title: Lindauer DORNIER GmbH - Quality creates value.
content:
Overview:
Lindauer DORNIER GmbH is an internationally active mechanical and plant engineering company with around 1,000 employees. Founded in 1950 by Peter Dornier, son of aviation pioneer Claude Dornier, the medium-sized family business with its three product lines - weaving machines, film stretching lines and composite systems - is today one of the global technology and market leaders. Customers from the textile and clothing industry use DORNIER air-jet and rapier weaving machines to produce fabrics for clothing, home textiles and technical textiles, including suits, wallpaper, firefighter clothing, airbags, tire cord, parachutes and filters. DORNIER is the world market leader in systems for the production of biaxially oriented polyester film (BOPET). These films are used in the packaging industry, particularly for food (including flexible packaging), pharmaceuticals and household products, as well as in solar cells, lithium-ion batteries, semiconductors, capacitors and in devices such as smartphones, smart TVs and tablets. In the Composite Systems (CS) division, DORNIER bundles its decades of experience in the construction of weaving machines and film stretching systems. With the machines and systems developed and built in CS, including the P2 roving weaving machine, the TRITOS® 3D weaving machine and the PROTOS® tape production line and tape weaving machine, DORNIER enables companies to achieve scalable and robust series production of technical textiles, composites and composite materials. All DORNIER machines and lines are “Made in Germany” and are developed, designed and built at the production sites in Lindau (headquarters) and Esseratsweiler. To ensure optimum local support, DORNIER has its own subsidiaries in the USA, China, India and Turkey. These subsidiaries enable us to be there for our customers directly in the most important markets worldwide.

title: 50 Years Brückner - World Market Leadership Strengthened
content: Over decades, not only was Brückner able to secure, but also to strengthen their position as world market leader for film stretching lines – within the entire BO market as well as in the BOPP segment. As to BOPET, Brückner has been able to gain a significant market share in recent years. For Brückner Maschinenbau, China has by far been the most important market for many years. Although a downturn is presently being observed for lines for standard packaging film in China, this shall, above all, be compensated by the demand for production lines for technical film (e.g. BOPET thick film). In Western Europe, USA, Japan, Taiwan and Korea, only a few large lines are being ordered to meet the slightly increased demand for standard film. At K 2010 the company presents new line concepts for more efficiency and sustainability in plastics film production as well as for the manufacture of trend-setting specialty films.

title: About us - Lindauer DORNIER GmbH
content: # Innovation and quality in mechanical engineering since 1950. For over 75 years, Lindauer DORNIER GmbH has stood for innovation, precision and the highest quality in mechanical engineering. As a family-owned company with an international reach, we set standards worldwide and develop machine solutions that ensure the success of our customers in a wide range of industries. Our commitment to quality and precision has made us a world leader in mechanical engineering. From weaving machines and film stretching systems to Composite Systems – our products stand for reliability and progress. With a clear focus on research, development and sustainability, DORNIER is shaping the future of the mechanical engineering industry. Our solutions are designed to meet the challenges of tomorrow and set new standards in efficiency and technology. With headquarters in Lindau on Lake Constance and other production and service locations worldwide, DORNIER has an international presence. Our products for the textile, plastics and specialty products industry are tailor-made to the requirements of our customers.
